jen_k: Heads up — we'd like to add a lightweight request context tag to console metrics so ops can correlate spikes to incoming request ids. Need alignment across runtime/infra/console. cc @aditya @sara_p @kevin

aditya: Quick q: do we want to propagate a single short header (x-rw-req) or use traceparent/trace-id? runtime can add header + tag to metrics, but spans may be sampled out.

mike_r: We should avoid sending full trace spans to metrics engine. Proposal: always emit an 8-char request_id as metric label, and separately emit distributed traces only when sampled. That lets dashboards drill down when traces exist. :+1:

sara_p: Infra concerns: cardinality. If we add request_id as label to p95 latency histograms that'll explode cardinality and kill storage. Suggest: use high-card request_id only on a 'request_events' counter stream, and for histograms keep route+model+tenant only. We can link via logs/trace lookup. :warning:

kevin: From console UX: we need clickable links from an invocation in the top-level chart to drill into traces or logs. If we emit a request_id in the event stream we can build drilldowns without adding it to histograms. Sounds like sara and mike's approach. :eyes:

aditya: ```
# runtime incoming request
req_id = req.headers.get("x-rw-req")
if not req_id:
  req_id = short_random()
metrics.emit("invocation_received", tags={"req_id": req_id, "route": route})
# For spans: set trace tag but only export spans when sampled
span.set_tag("rw.req", req_id)
```

mike_r: Sampling policy: keep current 1% global, but add 'on_error' and 'high-latency' triggers to force-sample. Runtime can set sampled=True when status>=500 or latency>1s. That gives traces when they're most useful.

sara_p: We'll add an aggregation pipeline: request_events -> log-index; a daily job that rollups request_id -> metrics only for top N frequent req ids. Also we can attach route/tenant tags for dashboards. Need an infra ticket.

jen_k: Plan: 1) runtime PR to add x-rw-req header + metric emit (aditya) 2) infra pipeline config for request_events (sara) 3) console drilldown UI to consume request_events (kevin) 4) rollout: feature flag on console + opt-in on prod for 2 weeks. Can folks comment if timeline ok?

kevin: Timeline: 2 weeks for UI quicklink prototype, ok.

aditya: I'll open PR tomorrow with opt-in env var RUNTIME_EMIT_REQ_EVENTS=true

sara_p: I'll file infra ticket and include retention & cardinality limits. Also adding rate-limit on req_events to 5000/s.

dashbot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for runtime change at 2027-05-03 15:00 UTC

jen_k: Thanks all. Creating tracking issue and will assign. :thumbsup:
